To dynamically resize the size of the text bubble in relation to how much text is displayed, you can utilize CSS flexbox properties combined with setting the width of the text bubble based on the content length. Here's how you can modify the code to achieve this:

```tsx
<View className="flex gap-y-3">
  {messages?.map((message) =>
    message.senderId === user.id ? (
      <View className="bg-dark-purple self-start rounded-xl px-4 py-3" style={{ maxWidth: `${message.content.length * 10}px` }} key={message.id}>
        <Text className="text-slate-200">{message.content}</Text>
      </View>
    ) : (
      <View className="bg-red-800 self-end rounded-xl px-4 py-3" style={{ maxWidth: `${message.content.length * 10}px` }} key={message.id}>
        <Text className="text-slate-200">{message.content}</Text>
      </View>
    )
  )}
</View>
```

In this code:

- I've changed the alignment of the bubbles so that the sender's bubbles align to the start, and the receiver's bubbles align to the end.
- I've added a `maxWidth` inline style to each bubble, which is calculated based on the length of the message content. You might need to adjust the `* 10` factor according to your layout requirements. This will dynamically adjust the width of the bubble based on the length of the text content.
